key_insight: This paper unifies several distributional training methods for one-step visual generation under a single theoretical framework. It shows that global distribution-matching objectives can be translated into pointwise feature updates via Wasserstein gradient flow.
problem_solved: One-step visual generation needs a principled way to train generators using distribution-level supervision in frozen feature spaces, while understanding how different matching losses relate to each other.
method: Formulates distributional training as a unified framework that separates distribution modeling from the choice of matching discrepancy.
Uses Wasserstein gradient flow to connect global objectives with pointwise feature updates.
Recovers existing methods such as FD-Loss and Gaussian-kernel Drifting through special cases like Gaussian optimal transport and kernel-density matching.
impact: For practitioners, this provides a clearer theoretical basis for designing and comparing one-step generation losses. It can help simplify method selection, improve interpretability, and guide new loss design for visual generation systems.
